title: Average Time Between Signups
scenario: Calculate the average time (in days) between a user's sign-up and their first confirmation request. Return the result table as 'avg_gap'.
tableSchema: signups (user_id INT, time_stamp DATETIME), confirmations (user_id INT, time_stamp DATETIME, action VARCHAR)
hint: Join signups and the minimum time_stamp from confirmations, then calculate the date difference.
correctQuery: SELECT AVG(JULIANDAY(c.min_time) - JULIANDAY(s.time_stamp)) AS avg_gap FROM signups s JOIN (SELECT user_id, MIN(time_stamp) AS min_time FROM confirmations GROUP BY user_id) c ON s.user_id = c.user_id;
setupSQL: CREATE TABLE signups (user_id INT, time_stamp DATETIME); CREATE TABLE confirmations (user_id INT, time_stamp DATETIME, action VARCHAR); INSERT INTO signups VALUES (3, '2020-03-21 10:16:13'); INSERT INTO confirmations VALUES (3, '2021-01-06 03:30:46', 'timeout');
